Question 1

What is the trace in the yz-plane of the hyperbolic paraboloid z−3=(x−5)25−y24?

a
A parabola: y2=4(z−3)
b
A hyperbola: 4x2−y2=1
c
Two intersecting lines: y=±4(x−3)
d
Two parallel lines: y=4(x±5)
e
A parabola: y2=−4(z−8)
Submit

decision.explanation: The yz-plane has x=0. Substituting gives z-3=25/5-y²/4=5-y²/4, so z-8=-y²/4 and y²=-4(z-8). This is a parabola.

after.problem: What is the trace in the $yz$-plane of the hyperbolic paraboloid $z-3=\frac{(x-5)^{2}}{5}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}?$
after.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $yz$-plane, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the paraboloid, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-3 & =\frac{(0-5)^{2}}{5}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} \\ z-3 & =\frac{25}{5}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} \\ z-3 & =5-\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} \\ z-8 & =-\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} \\ {y}^{2} & =-4(z-8)\end{aligned}
$$

 

This gives us the equation of the parabola in $yz$-plane.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Given the elliptic paraboloid $z+4=\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-4)^{2}}{4}$, find its intercepts with the $x$-axis.
after.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the paraboloid, we substitute $y=0$ and $z=0$ into the equation of the paraboloid and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}0+4 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(0-4)^{2}}{4} \\ 4 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{16}{4} \\ 4 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+4 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{4} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the solution $x=0$

Therefore, the intercept with the $x$-axis is $(0,0,0)$ only.

after.problem: Find the saddle point of the hyperbolic paraboloid $z+8={x}^{2}-(y+9)^{2}.$
after.worked_solution:
The general equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid with a saddle point at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is 

$$
z-{z}_{0}=\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}}.
$$

To find the saddle point, we rewrite our equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}z+8 & ={x}^{2}-(y+9)^{2} \\ z-(-8) & =\frac{(x-0)^{2}}{1}-\frac{(y-(-9))^{2}}{1}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid with a saddle point at $(0,-9,-8).$

after.problem: Find the saddle point of the hyperbolic paraboloid $z+4=\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{2}-\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{3}.$
after.worked_solution:
The general equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid with a saddle point at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is 

$$
z-{z}_{0}=\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}}.
$$

To find the saddle point, we rewrite our equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}z+4 & =\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{2}-\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{3} \\ z-(-4) & =\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{2}-\frac{(y-(-1))^{2}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid with a saddle point at $(3,-1,-4).$

after.problem: What is the trace in the $xz$-plane of the hyperbolic paraboloid $z+2=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{3}?$
after.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $xz$-plane, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the paraboloid, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}z+2 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{(0+3)^{2}}{3} \\ z+2 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{9}{3} \\ z+2 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-3 \\ z+5 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2} \\ {x}^{2} & =2(z+5)\end{aligned}
